title: Holiday Gift Card Marketing for Med Spas and Day Spas
seoTitle: Spa Gift Card Marketing: A 2026 Holiday Plan
seoDescription: A dated plan for selling med spa and day spa gift cards through December 24, 2026, what gift card rules say, and how to turn January visits into clients.
excerpt: Gift card season for spas starts now. Here is a dated plan through December 24, how to package medical treatments safely, and how to turn January visits into repeat clients.
imageAlt: Gift box wrapped in green paper with a peach satin ribbon and a sprig of eucalyptus, with more wrapped gifts behind it
imageIdea: Elegant wrapped gift with eucalyptus in soft neutral tones, no logos or readable text.
author: The SocialDM Insights Team
bodyHtml:
Spa gift card marketing works best as a plan with dates, not a single post in December. Decide what you sell, put it where buyers already look, push it on the days that matter, and get ready for January, when recipients walk in for the first time. Much of a gift card's value shows up after the holidays, not at checkout.

Below is a plan through December 24, 2026, plus what to do with redemptions in early 2027.

Why plan gift cards now instead of in December?

Because buyers start early and the calendar is tight. The National Retail Federation forecasts that U.S. retail sales in November and December 2026 will grow 4.2% over 2025 to $1.013 trillion (a figure that excludes auto dealers, gas stations and restaurants). Gift cards are a big piece of holiday giving: for the 2025 season, NRF reported that 43% of shoppers planned to buy at least one gift card, that gift cards ranked as the second most popular gift, and that gift card spending was expected to reach $29 billion.

Those are national retail numbers, not spa numbers, but the habit is there.

What should a spa gift card actually be?

Offer two kinds and keep the menu short: dollar value cards and a few named experiences. Too many options slow a buyer down, and a buyer who hesitates may close the tab.

FormatBest forWatch out for
Dollar value card (for example $100, $150, $250)Med spas, buyers who do not know the recipient's preferences, anything medicalCan feel less personal; add a short card message and a suggested treatment list
Named spa experience (for example a signature facial or a massage and facial pairing)Day spas, partners and parents who want to give "the experience"Prices change in 2027; decide now whether the card covers the service or its value at purchase, and say so in the terms
Consultation plus credit (a consultation with a dollar credit toward treatment)Med spas that want to gift aesthetic care safelyThe recipient may not be a candidate for what the buyer had in mind; the credit has to work for other services

Why medical treatments need extra care

A buyer can give a facial. A buyer cannot decide that someone else should get injectables, laser resurfacing or any other medical treatment. The recipient needs a consultation, and a licensed provider has to decide whether they are a good candidate. Some people will not be.

So for medical services, we would avoid cards named after a specific injectable treatment. Sell a dollar value or a consultation plus credit card instead, and say plainly on the card and the checkout page: "Treatments are subject to a consultation and provider approval. If a treatment is not right for you, your balance can be used for other services." Have your medical director approve that wording, and check your state's rules on advertising and selling medical services with your attorney.

Keep the marketing about the gift and the experience, not results. The FTC's Health Products Compliance Guidance says health related claims need competent and reliable scientific evidence. "Give her time for herself" is safe. "Give her ten years back" is a promise you cannot keep.

What do gift card rules require?

There is a federal floor, and many states go further. This is a summary for planning, not legal advice, so have an attorney review your terms before you sell.

  • Five years before funds expire. The Federal Reserve's 2010 gift card rules under the CARD Act say expiration dates for funds underlying gift cards must be at least five years after the card is issued (or, for reloadable cards, after funds were last loaded).
  • Limits on dormancy and inactivity fees. The same rules allow such fees only if the card has not been used for at least one year, no more than one fee is charged per month, and the fees are clearly disclosed.
  • Disclosures on the card. The regulation, 12 CFR 1005.20, says required disclosures must appear on the card itself, including the expiration date of the funds or a statement that they do not expire.
  • Promotional cards are different. The same section treats cards issued as part of a loyalty, award or promotional program separately. If you run "buy $200, get a $25 bonus card," the bonus card needs to say on its front that it is promotional and show its expiration date. Keep paid cards and bonus cards visually distinct.
  • State rules can be stricter. California's Civil Code section 1749.5, for example, generally makes it unlawful to sell a gift certificate with an expiration date. Other states have their own rules on fees, cash back for small balances and unclaimed balances.

What is the 2026 gift card calendar?

Thanksgiving is Thursday, November 26. That sets up the key dates below.

DateWhat it isWhat to do
Nov 16 to 20SetupFinalize the card menu and terms, test checkout on a phone, add a gift card button to your homepage and menu, set holiday hours on Google
Nov 16 to 25Early buyersTell your current clients first; publish your Google offer post and pin an Instagram post
Fri, Nov 27Black FridayLaunch any bonus offer; email in the morning, Instagram stories through the day
Sat, Nov 28Small Business SaturdayIn person sales: a gift card display at the front desk, wrapped physical cards ready to go
Mon, Nov 30Cyber MondayA short email: "Send a spa gift card in two minutes"
Tue, Dec 1GivingTuesdayA thank you post, or a donated gift card for a local cause. Ask your attorney before tying sales to a donation, since charity promotions can carry their own rules
Dec 17 to 19Mailing cutoffsUSPS recommends sending by Dec 17 (Ground Advantage and First Class Mail), Dec 18 (Priority Mail) or Dec 19 (Priority Mail Express) for delivery by Dec 25 in the contiguous U.S. Stop promising mailed cards after your cutoff
Dec 22 to 24Last minute buyersSwitch every message to e gift cards and same day pickup; post daily on Google and Instagram

Where should your gift cards show up?

Everywhere a buyer already looks, with the same price and terms in each place.

Your Google Business Profile

Use an offer post. Google's posts help page says offer posts need a title, dates and a time, and you can add a description, photo, coupon code, link and terms. Set the date range from launch through December 24 so the post stays current. Link straight to your gift card page, not your home page. Add an update post in the last week with the e gift card message.

Set special hours for Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Year's Eve and New Year's Day. A last minute buyer who drives over and finds you closed may not try again. Our post on how clients choose a med spa online covers the rest of your profile.

Your website

  • A "Gift Cards" button in the main menu and on the homepage from now through December 24.
  • One gift card page with the menu, terms in plain language, delivery options and the consultation note for medical services.
  • Checkout that works on a phone in under two minutes. Time it yourself.
  • An option to schedule e gift card delivery for a chosen date, and a field for the recipient's email so you can welcome them later.

Instagram

Post the card, the room and the people. Four posts that work:

  1. A styled photo of the physical card with a robe or wrapped box.
  2. A short video walking through a treatment room, with a caption about what a first visit feels like.
  3. "What our team would gift": each provider names a favorite nonmedical service.
  4. A countdown story on Dec 22, 23 and 24: "Still time. E gift cards arrive in minutes."

End every post with the same instruction: "Tap the link in our bio for gift cards."

What should your messages say?

Short, warm, one link. Three you can adapt:

  • Client email, week of Nov 16: "You know us. Now you can share us. Holiday gift cards are live, in any amount or as one of our signature experiences. Send one by email in a couple of minutes, or pick up a wrapped card at the front desk."
  • Black Friday: "From today through [date], every $200 gift card comes with a $25 bonus card for you. Bonus cards are promotional and expire on [date]." (Check the bonus terms with your attorney first.)
  • Dec 23 text to clients who opted in: "Still need a gift? Our e gift cards arrive instantly and can be scheduled for Christmas morning. [link]"

How do you turn January redemptions into repeat clients?

Treat every gift card recipient as a new client you did not have to find. Plan the welcome now, before the cards go out.

  1. Tag the booking. Mark every gift card visit in your booking system so you can count first visits and rebookings in 2027.
  2. Brief the front desk. A simple script: "Welcome, this was a gift from someone who thinks a lot of you. Is this your first time with us? Let me show you around."
  3. Explain the consultation. For medical services, tell the recipient at booking that the first step is a consultation and that their balance works for other services if a treatment is not a fit.
  4. Offer the next visit before they leave. Not a hard sell. "Would you like to hold a time next month?" is enough.
  5. Follow up within a few days. A thank you message, a request for honest feedback and a way to join your list. Ask for reviews the same way you ask every client.
  6. Remind people with balances. If a card has money left, a friendly note in March helps the recipient come back. Check with your attorney on how to handle balances under your state's rules.

How do you plan gift cards for 2027?

Write down what sold, in what amounts, and on which days, then reuse the plan. Valentine's Day falls on Sunday, February 14, 2027, and Mother's Day on Sunday, May 9, 2027. Both are gift card moments for spas. If your page, Google post template and scripts are ready now, each of those campaigns gets much easier.

Questions we hear

When should a spa start selling holiday gift cards?

Now. Set up your card menu, terms and online checkout by November 20, tell your current clients first, then push on Black Friday (November 27, 2026), Small Business Saturday (November 28), Cyber Monday (November 30) and the last minute days of December 22 to 24.

Can a med spa sell gift cards for injectables?

It is safer to sell a dollar value or a consultation plus credit card than a card named after a specific injectable. The recipient needs a consultation and a provider has to decide whether they are a candidate. State on the card that the balance can be used for other services, and check your state's rules with your medical director and attorney.

Do spa gift cards have to last five years?

Under the federal CARD Act rules, the funds on a gift card generally cannot expire sooner than five years after the card is issued, and dormancy fees are limited. Some states are stricter; California, for example, generally bars expiration dates on gift certificates. Have an attorney review your terms.

Can a bonus gift card expire sooner than a paid one?

Federal rules treat promotional cards separately, but the card has to say on its front that it is promotional and show its expiration date. State rules may differ, so confirm your bonus terms with an attorney before you advertise them.

takeaways: Set up your gift card menu, terms and phone friendly checkout in mid November, then push on November 27, 28 and 30 and again on December 22 to 24.
For medical treatments, sell a dollar value or consultation plus credit card, because the recipient needs a consultation and may not be a candidate.
